record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.context_brief: Evolution and stability of highly compact solutions
record.original_question: Are the highly compact stationary axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov solutions stable under time evolution, and how can the very high spatial resolution needed to construct those stationary solutions be transferred to an evolution code so that simulations of their stability or collapse are practically feasible?

evidence.quote: The question of their stability, and more generally, the fate of any axially symmetric initial data requires an evolution code.
The highly compact solutions that were constructed in [3] require very high resolution. It is an outstanding problem to determine whether or not these solutions are stable.
How can the high resolution needed for the stationary solution be carried over to the evolution problem to make a simulation practically feasible?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein-Vlasov system in general relativity, in which a collisionless ensemble of particles is described by a non-negative distribution function f on the cotangent bundle of a four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime (M,g), satisfying the Vlasov equation along the geodesic flow of g, while the metric g satisfies the Einstein field equations with stress-energy tensor T_{μν} obtained as the momentum-space moment of f. Restrict attention to axially symmetric spacetimes, i.e. those admitting a spacelike Killing vector field with closed orbits, and consider stationary solutions of this system (admitting in addition a timelike Killing vector field) that are highly compact, meaning that the ratio 2M/R of twice the ADM mass to a suitable areal radius approaches the Buchdahl-type limit, and which have been constructed numerically only at very high spatial resolution.

(a) Determine whether such highly compact stationary axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov configurations are dynamically stable under perturbations evolved by the full nonlinear axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov evolution equations, or whether they instead undergo gravitational collapse or dispersion.

(b) Devise a numerical evolution scheme (or analytic framework) capable of inheriting the very high spatial resolution required to resolve such stationary solutions, so that simulations of their evolution—and in particular their stability or collapse—are computationally feasible.
artifact.status_search_result: The stability of highly compact stationary axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov solutions is explicitly described as an outstanding open problem; no published evolution-code study resolving these highly compact configurations appears in the literature, and the transfer of the required high spatial resolution to an evolution code remains unresolved.
